name: Jathniel
overview: Jathniel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the fourth-born son of Meshelemiah. His position within the Levitical lineage situates him within the priestly and service-oriented tribe of Israel. There are no additional notes or details about his life or roles beyond this genealogical information.
namesAndTitles: The name Jathniel means 'G-d hires' or 'G-d is forever,' reflecting a theocentric understanding consistent with Hebrew naming traditions. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:2, underscores a recognition of God's sovereignty and eternal nature, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Jathniel was the son of Shallum (Meshelemiah), establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text for Jathniel.
scriptureSignificance: Jathniel's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Levi, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical families responsible for religious duties in Israel. As the fourth son of Meshelemiah, he represents a link in the priestly heritage that was vital for the worship and service to God as outlined in the Old Testament. His mention in 1 Chronicles 26:2 highlights the importance of preserving the record of Levitical descendants for maintaining the order and function of temple service.
